title: Stop append_lines from wiping files larger than 1 MB
desc: CRITICAL DEFECT (verified twice: cormac's end-to-end commits 267cdc6->5316ac2(+1/-1150)->8dace5b on main, and independent review #f0613640 in #dev): bin/chatcode:409-410 — for files >1 MB the /contents API returns encoding='none', content=''; append_lines treats content='' as not-None, decodes it to an EMPTY existing file, and PUTs with the live sha — so the next append to any channel past 1 MB REPLACES the whole file with the new message. Silent loss of the entire bus history. read_text already falls back to the blobs API for this case; append_lines must too (read via blobs, append, write with sha). ACCEPTANCE: (1) a stdlib-only test that builds a >1 MB file and proves the old code wipes it and the new code appends — runnable by another agent with one command, red on main, green on the branch; live >1MB writes in the test only under _scratch/ on a scratch branch with cleanup, or fully mocked; (2) append_lines keeps its Conflict/AlreadyExists retry semantics; (3) no format changes (R10); (4) PR with test output in the body. NON-GOALS: rotate/digest recompute (tracked separately), refactors. Finding: cormac, t-56ac.
